bearerAuth.description:
Send your token as `Authorization: Bearer sona_...`.

Tokens are shown once when created and stored hashed, so a lost token
cannot be recovered. Revoke it and make another.

info.description:
Read and manage your sona.to account from your own scripts and tools.

Every request needs a bearer token. Create one under API in your dashboard.
A token belongs to one team and can only ever reach that team's data.

## Connect an AI assistant (MCP)

sona.to runs a Model Context Protocol server at `https://mcp.sona.to/mcp`.
It exposes the same account, channels, posts, analytics and SEO actions as
tools an AI client can call, scoped to your team. Any MCP-compatible client
can connect, including Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor and others.

**Clients that support OAuth (Claude, ChatGPT and others).** Add a custom
connector with the URL above. You sign in with sona.to and approve access.
No token to paste.

**Clients that use a header (Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf and others).**
Create a token in the dashboard and pass it as a bearer header, for example:
`claude mcp add sona --transport http --header "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://mcp.sona.to/mcp`

Write actions (creating posts, uploads, running SEO audits and AI Visibility checks) require a token
or connection granted the write scope. Read access is always available.

## Uploading a file

To attach an image or video that is already at a public URL, pass that URL
straight to the create-post action. To upload a file the client holds
locally, use the two upload tools. Call the create-upload tool with the
filename and size to get a short-lived URL, PUT the raw bytes to that URL,
then call the finalize tool with the returned reference. Finalize stores
the file against your team and returns its public URL, which the create-post
action then accepts. The bytes go straight to storage and never pass through
the tool call.

## Webhooks

Instead of polling, have sona.to call you when something happens. Point a
webhook at Zapier, Make, n8n or your own server and choose which events it
receives.

The destination must use `https` on port 443 and resolve to a public
address. Redirects are not followed, so give the final URL.

**Verifying a delivery.** Every request carries a `Sona-Signature` header:

`Sona-Signature: t=1785935116,v1=d3d9c2c387bf7556...`

`t` is the unix time the request was signed and `v1` is an HMAC SHA-256 of
the timestamp, a full stop, then the raw request body, keyed with the
signing secret shown when you created the webhook. Recompute it and compare
with a constant-time function. Reject anything whose timestamp is more than
a few minutes old, which is what stops a captured request being replayed.

```php
$raw = file_get_contents('php://input');
preg_match('/t=(\d+),v1=([a-f0-9]{64})/', $_SERVER['HTTP_SONA_SIGNATURE'], $m);
[, $ts, $sig] = $m;

if (abs(time() - (int) $ts) > 300) { http_response_code(400); exit; }

$expected = hash_hmac('sha256', $ts . '.' . $raw, $secret);
if (!hash_equals($expected, $sig)) { http_response_code(401); exit; }
```

**Retries.** Any response outside 2xx, or no response within ten seconds, is
a failure. A failed delivery is retried after 60 seconds, then 5 minutes,
then 30 minutes, and abandoned after that. Reply 2xx as soon as you have the
payload and do your work afterwards.

Each delivery carries a `Sona-Delivery` id that stays the same across
retries of the same event, so you can ignore duplicates.

An endpoint that fails repeatedly is disabled automatically. Re-enable it
from the dashboard or by sending `status: true` to the update endpoint.

## AI Visibility

AI Visibility asks AI assistants the questions your customers ask and
records whether they name your brand, at which position and which sites
they cite. Add prompts, start a run, then read the overview, prompts,
sources and actions. A run uses AI credits for each answer received;
scheduled runs use fewer credits per answer than runs started now.

Webhook events follow each run. `seo.ai_visibility.completed` carries the
project, the run and its metrics. `seo.ai_visibility.failed` is sent when no
assistant returned an answer. `seo.ai_visibility.mention_gained` and
`seo.ai_visibility.mention_lost` list, in `mentions`, the prompt and
assistant pairs whose result changed since that pair was last asked, at
most 100 per event with the full count in `total`.

get.description:
Daily metrics for a connected channel over a date range, read from
stored data. Values are refreshed on a schedule, so this never triggers
a live fetch from the network.

Each metric carries its full daily `series`, plus `latest` and `sum`.
The `aggregation` field says which of the two is the meaningful total:
`latest` for a running count like followers, `sum` for per-day activity
like impressions. Where the right choice is genuinely ambiguous,
`aggregation` and `total` are null and both `latest` and `sum` are still
given, so you decide.

post.description:
Upload one or more files and get back a url for each. Pass those urls in
the `media` array of a post to publish them.

Send the files as multipart form data under the repeated field `files[]`.
Uploads count against your plan's storage and appear in your Files, the
same as a file added from the dashboard.

This endpoint accepts files up to 100 MB. Anything larger is rejected
before it reaches us, with an error that does not come from this API. Use
`POST /files/presign` for bigger files.

Allowed types and the per-file size limit also come from your plan, and
may be lower than 100 MB. A file of a disallowed type, one over your
plan's limit, or one that would take you past your storage allowance is
rejected with a message saying which.

Requires the `write` scope.

Step two of a two step upload. Call this after the PUT has completed.
Checks the file landed, measures its real size and type against your
plan, and records it in your Files.
Returns the same shape as `POST /files`, so the `url` can go straight
into the `media` array of a post.
Requires the `write` scope.

upload_ref.description: The value returned by the presign step.

post.x-curl:
curl -X POST https://api.sona.to/v1/files/finalize \\
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sona_your_token" \\
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\
  -d '{"upload_ref":"example01"}'

post.description:
Step one of a two step upload, for files over the 100 MB limit on
`POST /files`. Returns a short lived url to send the raw bytes to with a
PUT, and an `upload_ref` to pass to the finalize step.

Send the bytes with a single PUT to `upload_url`, including any headers
returned in `headers`. They go straight to storage rather than through
this API, so the 100 MB limit does not apply. The ceiling here is your
plan's per-file limit, returned as `max_bytes`.

The url expires after `expires_in` seconds, which scales with the size
you declare: 15 minutes plus a minute per 10 MB, up to an hour. An
expired url returns 403 from storage, not from this API. Nothing is
recorded in your Files until you call finalize.
Requires the `write` scope.

filename.description: Name to store the file under.

size_bytes.description: Size of the file in bytes. Must be positive.

expires_in.description: Seconds until the upload url expires.

headers.description: Headers to include on the PUT.

max_bytes.description: Largest file this token may upload.

upload_ref.description: Pass this to the finalize step.

upload_url.description: Send the raw bytes here with a PUT.

post.x-curl:
curl -X POST https://api.sona.to/v1/files/presign \\
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sona_your_token" \\
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\
  -d '{"filename":"clip.mp4","size_bytes":734003200,"content_type":"video/mp4"}'

post.description:
Creates one post per channel. Without `scheduled_at` the post goes out
immediately and the response carries the result. With `scheduled_at` the
post is queued and published at that time.

Either every channel accepts the post or none of them do. If any channel
fails validation the whole request is rejected, so a partial publish can
never happen without you knowing.

Requires the `write` scope.

delete.description:
Removes a post that has not gone out. A published post returns 409,
since deleting the record would not recall the message.

Requires the `write` scope.

patch.description:
Only a post still waiting to go out can be changed. A published post, a
failed one, or one already being sent returns 409.

Only the fields you send are touched, so changing the time leaves the
caption alone.

Requires the `write` scope.

get.description:
How often AI assistants (ChatGPT, Gemini, Google AI Mode, Google AI
Overviews, Perplexity and Claude) name the brand when asked the tracked
prompts, from the latest finished run: visibility, share of voice,
average position, results per assistant, the brands named most and the
trend over recent runs. `metrics` is null until a run has finished.

`credits_run_now` is the most a run started now would use. A check that
fails costs nothing, so a run often uses less.

AI Visibility must be included in the plan. Without it, every AI
Visibility endpoint returns 403 `plan_required`.

Changes that can get the brand into more answers, rebuilt after every
run. `kind` is one of:

`crawler_blocked` robots.txt stops an assistant's crawler from reading
the site. `details` lists the crawlers and paths.

`no_mention` no assistant names the brand on a prompt. `details` lists
the brands named instead.

`source_gap` a site that several assistants cite on prompts where the
brand is absent. `details` gives the domain, an example page and the
brands it names.

Done actions carry `measure`: visibility on the action's prompts on the
run before it was marked done, and on the latest run since.

The latest answer from each assistant for one prompt: the answer text in
Markdown, whether the brand is named and at which position, the brands
named in order, the sources cited and the searches the assistant ran.
`history` gives mentioned or not per assistant over the last runs that
asked this prompt, oldest first.

An answer with status `empty` means the assistant showed no AI answer for

post.description:
Ask every tracked prompt on every selected assistant now, or only the
prompts in `prompt_ids`. Returns straight away; poll
`GET /seo/projects/{id}/ai-visibility/runs/{runId}` until `status` reads
done or failed, or subscribe to the `seo.ai_visibility.completed`
webhook. A run of a few prompts usually takes one to two minutes.

Uses AI credits for each answer received. `credits_max` is the most the
run can use; checks that fail cost nothing. One run at a time per
project: starting another while one is queued or running returns 409.

Requires the `write` scope.

patch.description:
Change which assistants are asked, the schedule, the brand name or the
other names the brand goes by. Fields not sent keep their value.
Answers are searched for the brand name and every other name, whole
words only and without case.

A scheduled run uses fewer credits per answer than a run started now.
Claude is asked at most once a week on a schedule.

Requires the `write` scope.

a brand named in the answers), `community`, `social`, `video`,
`reference` or `editorial`. `your_pages` lists the pages of your site
cited over the last four runs.

Queue a crawl and analysis for the project. Returns straight away with
the status set to queued; poll `GET /seo/projects/{id}` and read

project, so calling this while one is queued or running returns 409.

Requires the `write` scope.

Generate a suggested fix for an issue. This runs an AI generation and
uses credits. It returns a before and after suggestion; you apply the
change on your own site. Not every issue type has an automatic fix, and
one that cannot be generated returns 422.

Requires the `write` scope.

get.description: Pages found in the last crawl, with their on-page SEO data.

The Google position of every keyword tracked for the project, from its
latest check. `position` is null when the site is not in the first
`limits.depth` results. `change` is the number of places gained since 7
days ago (daily plans) or since the previous check (weekly plans):
positive means the site climbed, `in` means it entered the checked depth,
`out` means it dropped out, null means there is not enough history.

Google can show different results to identical searches. When a check
moves a keyword a lot, a second search confirms it. When the two
disagree, the position where the site was found is kept and `unstable`
is true.

`features` lists what the results page shows: `aio` (AI Overview),
`aio_you` (the AI Overview cites the site, plans with AI Visibility),
`snippet`, `snippet_you`, `local`, `video`, `paa` (People also ask),
`shopping`, `news`, `images`.

The Rank Tracker must be included in the plan. Without it, every Rank
Tracker endpoint returns 403 `plan_required`.

post.description:
Track Google searches for one country, language and device. The first
check runs within minutes. Keywords already tracked with the same
country, language and device are skipped.

The plan sets how many keywords a team tracks across its sites and how
many it can add in any 7 days. Deleting a keyword does not give the
addition back. Keywords past either limit are not added and are counted
in `skipped_over_limit`. Returns 201 when at least one keyword was added,
200 when every keyword was already tracked.

Requires the `write` scope.

language.description: Google language code, for example en, fr, de, pt, zh-CN.

409.description: `busy` keywords are being added for this team. Try again in a moment.

422.description:
`invalid_keywords`, `invalid_country`, `invalid_language` or `invalid_device`.
`limit_reached` the plan has no keyword places left.
`additions_limit` the team added its plan's keyword count in the last 7 days.

delete.description:
The keyword and its position history are deleted.

Requires the `write` scope.

get.description:
One keyword with its position history (one point per check, unstable
checks left out), its best position, the domains in the latest top 10
with their position at the check before, the domains the AI Overview
cites, and Search Console impressions and clicks from the latest pull.

post.description:
Checks the Google position now instead of waiting for the scheduled
check. Uses `check_now_credits` AI credits, charged once when the result
is stored. The result is usually ready within 3 minutes; read it with the
keyword endpoint, where `checking` is false once it is stored.

Requires the `write` scope.

402.description: `insufficient_credits` the team does not have enough AI credits left.

409.description: `busy` a check is already running for this keyword.

post.description:
The signing secret is returned once, in this response, and cannot be
retrieved afterwards. Store it before you close the connection.

The URL must use https on port 443 and must resolve to a public
address. Redirects are not followed.

422.description:
`invalid_url` the destination was rejected.
`invalid_events` an unknown event was named.
`limit_reached` the team already has the maximum number of webhooks.

data.description: A site audit failed to complete.
data.name: seo.audit.failed

data.description: An AI Visibility check failed: no assistant returned an answer.
data.name: seo.ai_visibility.failed

data.description: An assistant named your brand on a prompt where it did not before.

data.name: seo.ai_visibility.mention_lost

patch.description:
Send only the fields you want to change. Setting status to true on a
webhook that was disabled after repeated failures also clears its
failure count.

get.description:
Newest first. Useful for diagnosing an endpoint that is failing.
History is kept for a limited period, not indefinitely.
